    Bounded length gives finitely many indecomposables #

    For a connected algebra with a preprojective component, if the indecomposables have bounded dimension then there are only finitely many of them up to isomorphism (finite_of_bounded, a first Brauer–Thrall statement in this setting): every indecomposable lies in the component, maps nonzero into an indecomposable summand of DA, and is therefore isomorphic to that summand or to one of its finitely many predecessors.
